name: Fork
mnemonic: One piece, two targets — they can only save one.
definition: A single piece attacks two or more enemy pieces at once. Knights are the classic forkers because their attack can't be blocked.
hint: Which square does the knight attack with check and also hit a rook?
explanation: Ne7+ checks the king and attacks the c8-rook at the same time. The e1-rook protects the knight, so after the king steps away White takes the rook — a rook for a knight (winning the exchange).

name: Pin
mnemonic: Frozen in place: moving would expose something bigger.
definition: A piece cannot move (or moving it would lose more) because a more valuable piece stands behind it on the same line. An absolute pin is against the king.
hint: Line up a bishop with the queen and the king on the long diagonal.
explanation: Bd4 pins the f6-queen to the h8-king along the a1–h8 diagonal. The queen can't step off the line, so the best Black can do is give it up for the bishop.

name: Skewer
mnemonic: A pin in reverse: the big piece is in front and must move.
definition: A line piece attacks a valuable piece, which must move and expose a piece behind it on the same line.
hint: Check the king along the 7th rank.
explanation: Ra7+ attacks the king; once it steps off the 7th rank, the rook runs through to h7 and takes the queen standing behind it.

name: Discovered attack
mnemonic: Move the curtain, reveal the gun.
definition: Moving one piece uncovers an attack by another piece behind it. Best when the moving piece also makes a threat — then the opponent faces two at once.
hint: The bishop stands between your rook and Black's queen.
explanation: Bxh7+ gives check, uncovering the d1-rook against the d6-queen. Black must answer the check, and the queen falls.

name: Double check
mnemonic: Two checks at once: the king must run.
definition: A discovered check where the moving piece also gives check. No block or capture can stop both checks, so the king must move — often into mate.
hint: Sacrifice the queen to drag the king onto the d-file.
explanation: Réti–Tartakower, Vienna 1910. Qd8+!! forces Kxd8; then Bg5+ is a double check from the bishop and the d1-rook. After Kc7, Bd8# finishes.

name: Deflection
mnemonic: Pull the guard away from its post.
definition: Force a defending piece away from the square or piece it protects, usually with a check or capture it must answer.
hint: The d8-rook is the queen's only defender. Give it something else to do.
explanation: Re8+ forces Rxe8 because there is no escape square. The rook is deflected from the d-file, so White's queen captures the undefended queen on d5.

name: Decoy
mnemonic: Lure the piece onto a poisoned square.
definition: A sacrifice that draws an enemy piece (often the king) onto a square where it can be hit by another tactic.
hint: Get the king onto h8, where a knight check can also hit d6.
explanation: Rh8+! decoys the king to h8. Now Nxf7+ forks king and queen, and White comes out a queen for a rook ahead.

name: Overloading
mnemonic: One defender, two jobs — it can't do both.
definition: A defending piece has more than one duty. Attack one of its charges and the other collapses.
hint: The c8-rook guards both the bishop and the back rank.
explanation: The c8-rook defends the c6-bishop and the d8 square. Qxc6! forces it to choose: if Rxc6, Rd8 is mate on the undefended back rank.

name: Interference
mnemonic: Block the line between a defender and what it defends.
definition: Place a piece on the line between an enemy piece and the square it protects, cutting the connection.
hint: The h8-rook guards c8 along the 8th rank. Get in its way.
explanation: Rd8! interrupts the h8-rook's control of c8. If Black captures, cxd8=Q promotes with a capture; if not, c8=Q comes next.

name: Zwischenzug
mnemonic: Before you recapture, look for a check.
definition: An 'in-between move': instead of the expected recapture, play a forcing move first (usually a check), then recapture.
goal: Win a pawn and the right to castle
hint: Black's queen isn't going anywhere — it's trapped on d1.
explanation: Black just took on d1. Rxd1 at once is natural, but Bxf7+ first grabs a pawn with check and drags the king into the open; the queen on d1 is still there to be taken.

name: Removing the defender
mnemonic: Kill the guard, take the castle.
definition: Capture or drive away the piece that defends a key square or piece.
hint: Only the f6-knight stops Qxh7 mate.
explanation: The queen and c2-bishop aim at h7, defended only by the f6-knight. Bxf6 removes it, and whatever Black recaptures with, Qxh7 is mate.

name: X-ray
mnemonic: Power passes through pieces on the same line.
definition: A piece attacks or defends a square through another piece on the same line. When the front piece is exchanged, the one behind takes over.
hint: Your rook on d1 is behind your queen on the d-file.
explanation: The d1-rook 'sees through' the queen to d8. Qxd8+ Rxd8 removes the defender, and the rook recaptures with back-rank mate.

name: Windmill
mnemonic: Check, capture, check, capture — the sails keep turning.
definition: A rook (or other piece) alternates between direct checks and discovered checks, grabbing material on every second move.
hint: The f6-bishop gives check every time the rook leaves g7.
explanation: Each time the rook leaves g7, the bishop gives a discovered check; each time it returns, the rook checks directly. Rxf7+, Rg7+ and Rxc7+ grab a pawn and then the queen.

name: Back-rank mate
mnemonic: No luft, no life: a king walled in by its own pawns.
definition: A rook or queen mates a king on its first rank whose escape is blocked by its own pawns.
hint: The b8-rook is the only guard of the back rank.
explanation: Qe8+! forces the rook to capture, and Rxe8 is mate because f7, g7 and h7 imprison the king. Always consider making 'luft' (h6 or g6) in time.
